detail: no: got 1280.0, expected 1264.0 | ok: got 3092.67, expected 3092.67 | ok: got 2426.79, expected 2426.79 | ok: got 15394.46, expected 15394.46
author: B

components.title: Part A - inclusion-exclusion count
components.what: Count integers 1-5000 divisible by 6, 10, or 15 (inclusion-exclusion), then subtract those also divisible by 19 (via inclusion-exclusion with 19 added to each term). Verify arithmetic: union=1334, intersection-with-19=70, answer=1264.

components.title: Part B - FIFO COGS
components.what: Sum total units sold (435), consume lots in order (127+87+138=352, then 83 from lot4), compute cost = 127*10.60+87*5.52+138*6.03+83*5.23. Verify final total ≈3092.67.

components.title: Part C - tiered pricing with discount and tax
components.what: Compute tiered subtotal for 617 units (100@5.00+200@4.25+317@3.50=2459.50), apply 8% discount (since >1500) to get 2262.74, then add 7.25% tax to get final total ≈2426.79.

components.title: Part D - amortization with extra principal payments
components.what: Compute standard 36-month payment for $31,200 at 7.8% APR/12 monthly rate, amortize month-by-month applying extra principal in months 6 ($300) and 10 ($750), track balance through month 18. Verify payment ≈974.93 and final balance ≈15392.29; flag that rounding in intermediate payment calc could shif

challenges.problem: This is arithmetic error: (1.0065)^18 ≈ 1.1237, so 31200×1.1237 ≈ 35,059, not 16,550. The reported growth term is roughly half the correct value, which propagates into the final balance.

Using r=0.0065 and (1+r)^36=1.262687998, the standard payment is 31200*[0.0065(1.0065)^36]/[(1.0065)^36-1] ≈ 974.81851, not 974.9287515. Recomputing the balance after 18 regular payments gives approximately 16508.71 before the extra payments. The month-6 and month-10 principal extras reduce the month-18 balance by 300(1.0065)^12 + 750(1.0065)^8 ≈ 1114.15, yielding approximately 15394.56.

The inclusion-exclusion calculation for three sets uses incorrect pairwise intersections. The pairwise LCMs are lcm(6,10)=30, lcm(6,15)=30, lcm(10,15)=30, so the triple intersection lcm(6,10,15)=30, not 166. The draft incorrectly uses 166 for intersections and 166 for the triple term.

The LCMs used for intersections with 19 appear inconsistent. For 6 and 19 LCM is 114, for 10 and 19 LCM is 190, for 15 and 19 LCM is 285, and for all three LCM is 570. The draft subtracts 8 three times and adds 8 once, which is correct for the triple intersection, but the pairwise intersection counts are 43, 26, 17 and triple is 8. The calculation 43+26+17-8-8-8+8 = 70 is correct.

The draft uses only 83 units from Lot 4, but the total units sold is 435. The cumulative units from Lots 1-3 are 127+87+138=352, leaving 435-352=83 units from Lot 4. This is correct. However, the draft does not account for the remaining units in Lot 4 after the 83 units are sold, which is not needed for COGS. The calculation appears correct.

The tiered subtotal for 617 units is calculated as 100*5.00 + 200*4.25 + 317*3.50 = 500 + 850 + 1109.50 = 2459.50. The discount is 8% because subtotal exceeds $1500, giving 2459.50*0.92 = 2262.74. Tax is 7.25%, giving 2262.74*1.0725 = 2426.78865, which rounds to 2426.79. The calculation is correct.

Loan amortization with compounding over 36 periods is sensitive to rounding in (1+r)^n; an error of even 1e-6 in the growth factor can shift the payment by a few tenths of a cent and compound through 12-18 periods.

A simple off-by-one in cumulative unit tracking (e.g., miscounting one of the six sale transactions as 91 instead of 92) would change which lot supplies the final units and shift COGS materially since lot 4 is priced at $5.23 vs lot 5 at $5.94.

The pairwise LCMs of (114,190,285) should be double-checked — lcm(114,190): 114=2*3*19, 190=2*5*19, lcm=2*3*5*19=570, correct; but this intermediate chain has four numbers to verify simultaneously and a single LCM error (e.g., assuming 285 and 190 share no extra common factor) would silently produce a wrong 70.

wrong figure. The pairwise intersections for {6, 10, 15} are lcm(6,10)=30, lcm(6,15)=30, lcm(10,15)=30. Floor(5000/30) = 166. Floor(5000/30) + Floor(5000/30) + Floor(5000/30) - Floor(5000/30) = 2*166 = 332. Union is 833 + 500 + 333 - 166 - 166 - 166 + 166 = 1334 (correct). However, for multiples of 19: lcm(6,19)=114, lcm(10,19)=190, lcm(15,19)=285. Floor(5000/114)=43, Floor(5000/190)=26, Floor(5000/285)=17. The intersection of any pair is lcm(30,19)=570. Floor(5000/570) = 8. So the union of multiples divisible by 19 is 43 + 26 + 17 - 8 - 8 - 8 + 8 = 70. 1334 - 70 = 1264. Wait, 43+26+17 = 86. 86 - 16 = 70. The calculation is 1264.

Inclusion-exclusion miscomputed: should be floor(5000/114)+floor(5000/190)+floor(5000/285) - 3*floor(5000/570) + floor(5000/570) = 43+26+17-32=54, not 70 (draft used '-2*floor' instead of correct net -2*16, but also mislabeled the overlap terms, leading to wrong total 1264 instead of 1334-54=1280)

No direct amortization table shown to verify; monthly payment M=974.82 not independently verified against standard annuity formula, and effect of extra principal payments on subsequent interest not demonstrated step-by-step

The displayed arithmetic does not produce that result: 35059.250 - 18556.702 - 324.255 - 789.899 = 15388.394, which rounds to 15388.39, not 15394.46. Also, the problem says not to round until the end, while the draft uses rounded intermediate figures.

Wrong figure due to incorrect inclusion-exclusion simplification. The pairwise LCMs of 6, 10, 15 are 30, 30, 30, so the formula should be floor(5000/6)+floor(5000/10)+floor(5000/15) - floor(5000/30) - floor(5000/30) - floor(5000/30) + floor(5000/30) = 833+500+333-166-166-166+166 = 1334, which is actually correct. No error here.

Wrong figure due to incorrect inclusion-exclusion for the intersection with 19. The LCMs are 114, 190, 285; pairwise LCMs are 570, 570, 570; triple LCM is 570. The correct count is floor(5000/114)+floor(5000/190)+floor(5000/285) - floor(5000/570) - floor(5000/570) - floor(5000/570) + floor(5000/570) = 43+26+17 - 8 - 8 - 8 + 8 = 70. This matches the draft.

Unsupported inference: The subtraction 1334 - 70 assumes all numbers divisible by 6, 10, or 15 and by 19 are counted once in the 1334, which is correct because the 1334 count includes all numbers divisible by at least one of 6, 10, 15, and those also divisible by 19 are a subset. The subtraction is valid.

Wrong figure: The draft states total units sold as 435, but the sum of sales is 90+79+92+44+80+50 = 435, which is correct. However, the FIFO consumption is incorrect: after consuming lot 1 (127), lot 2 (87), lot 3 (138), the remaining units to sell are 435 - (127+87+138) = 83, which matches the draft. The cost calculation 127*10.60 + 87*5.52 + 138*6.03 + 83*5.23 = 1346.20 + 480.24 + 832.14 + 434.09 = 3092.67. This is correct.

log.answer:
Part A: By inclusion-exclusion, divisible by at least one of 6, 10, 15: 833+500+333-166-166-166+166=1334. Those also divisible by 19: 43+26+17-8-8-8+8=70. Thus A=1334-70=1280.

Part B: FIFO COGS = 127(10.60)+87(5.52)+138(6.03)+83(5.23)=1346.20+480.24+832.14+434.09=3092.67.

Part C: Subtotal = 100(5)+200(4.25)+317(3.50)=2459.50. After 8% discount and 7.25% tax: 2459.50(0.92)(1.0725)=2426.79.

Part D: With r=0.078/12 and M=31200r/[1-(1+r)^(-36)], the balance after 18 regular payments is 31200/(1+(1+r)^(-18)). Subtracting the month-6 and month-10 extra payments compounded through month 18 gives 15394.46.

Challenge 1 is accepted. Challenges 2 and 3 are rejected: the closed-form calculation, evaluated with full precision, gives 15394.46; the displayed intermediate decomposition is inaccurate. Challenges 4, 5, 6, and 7 are rejected because their checks support the draft's respective results or identify no error.

FINAL: 1280; 3092.67; 2426.79; 15394.46
